industry.key: P. Energy, commodities and metals mining
industry.why: Overweight, carried. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: B now, A prior at the industry, with Downstream distribution A, Upstream A, Services D and Metals and mining F inside it. No Brent level reached the pack, so the condition (Brent under $85) is untested, and the undated headline that oil is dipping on peace hopes is noted, not acted on. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only): energy is still the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else, and the hedge has not been needed for two weeks. Eight of the top 40 on the starting score are energy names, from 15 last week, as Neste and Galp left the Pool. Counter-case: the tilt scorecard's negative spreads are consistent with the Overweight having been paid already, and a ceasefire would take the premium out. To C if Brent is read under $85 or the industry's relative strength falls to C.

sector.why: Neutral, carried, with the disagreement stated both ways and the copper headline added. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: F now, A prior on the two-month base, the same fall as the readings before it; the condition 'to D on a third reading at F' is met only if the 30-Oct-26 reading, which this week's file does not show, was also F, so I do not fire it on an inference. Against the tape: copper at a record on supply-squeeze fears (Marketscreener and SunSirs, undated; Goldman Sachs' December 2025 preference for copper) is the first commodity read supporting the demand side since DNB Carnegie's mining-cycle call. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). No Metals and mining name is in this week's candidate list. Counter-case: a group that has gone from A to F in two months is the market's view, and industrial metals into a growth scare is still the cyclical call. To D on a further F with the copper rally reversing or a dated mining read that fails; to B if relative strength leaves F with a dated copper read.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.
